newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures stumble lower as yen firms.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures stumble lower as yen firms.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock futures ended weaker on Thursday with the yen's strength spurring sales in line with the softer cash market, dealers said.
The yen's strength triggered sales of export-related shares on the underlying Tokyo stock market, which dragged futures down below the psychological 20,000 points support.
"Many Japanese exporters didn't hedge against the dollar/yen and were caught off guard when it fell," a dealer with a Japanese commission house said.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract fell 200 points to 20,045 at the close, on a turnover of 14,770 lots.
Dealers said the Nikkei was undergoing a healthy correction after recent strong gains and could resume its uptrend depending on volatility in the dollar/yen.
The dollar came under massive pressure in Asian currency markets on Thursday falling more than one yen to a four-month low of 115.60. At 0815 GMT, the dollar recouped to 116.10/6.14 yen.
The Nikkei was seen likely to consolidate ahead of the weekend with next support assessed at 19,800 points.
Meanwhile, the May MSCI Taiwan index contract fell 5.9 points to 336.7 fuelled by jitters over political stability in Taiwan.
